div.head: Wi 8
div.ab: Gif man his mæn an wiofode freols gefe, se sie folcfry; freolsgefa age his erfe ænde wergeld ⁊ munde þare hina, sie ofer mearce ðær he wille.
Gif man his mæn an wiofode freols gefe, se sie folcfry; freolsgefa age his erfe ænde wergeld ⁊ munde þare hina, sie ofer mearce ðær he wille.
Gif man his mæn an wiofode freols gefe, se sie folcfry; freolsgefa age his erfe ænde wergild ⁊ munde þare hina, sie ofer mearce ðær he wille.

Wenn jemand seinem [unfreien] Manne am Altare die Freiheit schenkt, [so] sei dieser volksfrei; der Freiheitschenker besitze [jedoch] dessen Erbe und Wergeld und Schutzrecht über die Familie [desselben, auch wenn] jener jenseits der Grenze lebt, wo er wolle.

If someone gives his [unfree] man freedom at the altar, [then] let the latter be folk-free; let the giver of freedom [however] have his inheritance and wergeld and the right of protection over [his] household, [even if] he lives beyond the border, wherever he wishes.

If anyone grants one of his men freedom on the altar, his freedom shall be publicly recognised; [but] the emancipator shall have his heritage and his wergeld, and the guardianship of his household, wherever he [the freed man] may be, [even if it be] beyond the border.

If anyone gives his man freedom at the altar, he is to have the rights of a freeman of that people; his manumittor is to have his inheritance and his wergild and protection over his household, even if he live beyond the boundary, wherever he wishes.

If a person sets his man free at the altar, he shall have the rights of a free man of the people; the freedomgiver owns his inheritance and wergeld and protection of the kin, let him [the newly freed man] be over the border wherever he wishes.

note.seg: Nicht Ein Wort: G. geaf freols Urk. 11. Jhs. Ke 925
Not a single word: G. geaf freols charter of the 11th cent., Ke 925
Vgl. Gl Erbgang 9a. Die Kinder werden mit dem Vater frei, im Ggs. zu Af El 11
Cf. Gl Erbgang 9a. The children become free together with the father, in contrast to Af El 11

Vgl. Hl 15³. Für die engste Bedeutung ‘Gutsbezirk des Freilassers’ spricht die Formel 11. Jhs., die den Mann clipað freon and saecles á (in) túne ⁊ of túne Thorpe Dipl. 622; vgl. die Befreiung ut of Toppesham lande, bezeugt vom Hundred at Toppeshamme 634; ut of Wunforda 631, ut of Seeftbeara 635. Doch berücksichtigte Wihtred wohl auch die nur der Person eines Herrn, nicht einem Landgut, untergebenen, grundbesitzlosen Unfreien. Für sie hiess ‘Grenze’ mindestens die des Gerichtsbezirkes, nicht bloss eines Herrschaftsguts. Es kann auch Kents Grenze gemeint sein, wenn z. B. der Freigelassene von einem Nachbarvolke stammte und im Kriege dort gefangen oder auf dem Londoner Sklavenmarkte angekauft war

Cf. Hl 15³. In favour of the narrowest meaning, ‘the manumitter’s estate’, speaks the 11th-cent. formula which clipað the man freon and saecles á (in) túne ⁊ of túne Thorpe Dipl. 622; cf. the manumission ut of Toppesham lande, attested by the Hundred at Toppeshamme 634; ut of Wunforda 631, ut of Seeftbeara 635. Yet Wihtred probably also took into account the landless unfree who were subject only to the person of a lord, not to an estate. For them ‘boundary’ meant at least that of the judicial district, not merely that of a manorial estate. Kent’s boundary may also be meant, if, e.g., the freedman came from a neighbouring people and had been captured there in war or bought in the London slave-market
The word occurs elsewhere only in II Can. cap. 45 § 1.
For ofer mearce cf. H. and E. cap. 15 and note; II Can. cap. 45 § 3.

note.seg: Strong parallels with clauses found in Frankish, Lombard, and Old Norse law indicate that §7 may contain oral-formulaic remnants from an earlier Germanic source. See discussion under ‘Manumission’ in Commentary.
